steps.name: CheckForScriptFile
steps.label: Check For Script File
steps.goal: Look the po.source_files for an .fdx file.  if we don't find one, we'll look for a .pdf.
steps.pass_criteria: we find a valid script file and add it to self.shared_data['script']
steps.fail_criteria: no valid script file is found.
steps.min_scenario: You hand-build the structure to the studio's convention — when the convention is clear and the inputs are present.
steps.max_scenario: The convention is undocumented or inconsistent across artists; you rebuild and reconcile it by hand.

steps.name: CreateScriptManifest
steps.label: Create Script Manifest
steps.goal: Create the script manifest from the self.shared_data['script'] file (Final Draft .fdx or screenplay .pdf; a PDF is parsed to a sibling .fdx first, then both follow the same path).
steps.pass_criteria: script.json + audit.json are written beside the source script.
steps.fail_criteria: no/unsupported script file, or no audit.json was created.
steps.min_scenario: You hand-build the structure to the studio's convention — when the convention is clear and the inputs are present.
steps.max_scenario: The convention is undocumented or inconsistent across artists; you rebuild and reconcile it by hand.

steps.name: ConfirmAudit
steps.label: Confirm Audit
steps.goal: Confirmt the audit.json exists and that there are no outstanding items left to process.
steps.pass_criteria: all items in list are marked as "confirmed": true
steps.fail_criteria: any items in the audit are marked as confirmed: false
steps.min_scenario: You eyeball the asset against the checklist by hand — naming, scale, topology, etc. — when it's clean and there's nothing to fix.
steps.max_scenario: You miss something (or there's a lot to fix); it ships, breaks in a downstream department, and bounces back days later for a re-publish.

steps.name: Publish
steps.label: Publish
steps.goal: run through the tpyical po.publish() process.
steps.min_scenario: You manually copy the version to the publish/latest location and a coordinator hand-updates the tracker and pings downstream — when everyone actually does their part.
steps.max_scenario: The coordinator's slammed and forgets (or no one notifies downstream); everyone waiting burns days on Slack, text, email, phone, and walking the building to find out if it's ready.

steps.name: AnalyzeScript
steps.label: Analyze Script
steps.goal: Read the just-published script and enrich the character / environment / prop registries from it, then write the first version of the crew documents (character profiles, location profiles, and the set-dressing / prop / lighting breakdown) to the render location.
steps.pass_criteria: character_profiles.md, location_profiles.md and breakdown.xlsx are written and the registries are enriched from the script.
steps.fail_criteria: the analysis raises before any document is produced.
steps.min_scenario: An AD or coordinator reads the whole script and types up character bios, a location breakdown and a prop / set-dressing / lighting spreadsheet by hand — fast when the script is short and they already know it.
steps.max_scenario: On a feature-length script it's days of reading and cross-referencing; details get missed or go stale the moment the script is revised, and the whole breakdown has to be redone.

steps.name: DeriveLocationStates
steps.label: Derive Location States
steps.goal: For every environment variation (state) the script implies, generate the character-free establishing-plate prompt that will produce its concept art — persist it on the env and append it to the location document.
steps.pass_criteria: each environment state has a plate prompt and location_profiles.md carries the Location State Plate Prompts appendix.
steps.fail_criteria: the derivation raises before any state is processed.
steps.min_scenario: A concept artist or AD writes an art-direction brief for each location and each time-of-day / condition variation by hand — quick for one or two clean sets.
steps.max_scenario: Across many sets and day / night / decay states it's a long manual pass, and the briefs drift from the script's actual scene coverage.

steps.name: DeriveCharacterLooks
steps.label: Derive Character Looks
steps.goal: Segment every character's scenes into wardrobe looks (costume changes tied to scenes), each with an estimated design prompt — persist them on the character and append them to the character document.
steps.pass_criteria: every character is processed (one default look, or per-scene looks) and character_profiles.md carries the Wardrobe Looks appendix.
steps.fail_criteria: the derivation raises before any character is processed.
steps.min_scenario: A costume designer reads the script and builds a costume plot — which outfit each character wears in which scene — by hand; quick when no one changes clothes.
steps.max_scenario: With costume changes, flashbacks and continuity states across a full cast it's a meticulous manual breakdown that's easy to get wrong and has to track every script revision.

steps.name: CreateSgProject
steps.label: Create SG Project
steps.goal: create shotgrid project on disk as part of alchemy project creation if this is a shotgrid project.
steps.min_scenario: You do the cleanup by hand before handing off — quick when you remember it.
steps.max_scenario: You forget or do it wrong; the mistake ships in the file and gets flagged downstream, forcing a redo.

steps.label: Audit Script

steps.name: ExtractLyrics
steps.label: Extract Lyrics
steps.goal: Transcribe a song file's sung vocals into the Script Editor: separates vocals (Demucs), runs local whisper, and seeds this version's transcript_edit.json (plus a plain <song>_lyrics.txt copy). Opens the Script Editor on the result.
steps.pass_criteria: transcript_edit.json is created for this version and shows in the Script Editor
steps.fail_criteria: no transcript created for this version

steps.name: CheckForReviewFiles
steps.label: Check For Review Files
steps.goal:
Locate the render image sequence to review (prefers ``playblast``) and
stash its printf pattern + frame range in shared_data for downstream steps.

steps.max_scenario: Settings are off or reviewers can't find it; you re-capture and re-share, and review slips.

trigger / UI before the recipe runs); we don't pop a dialog here. Falls
back to a sensible default so the review never blocks.
